how_it_was_refuted: I wrote the 'shared language' module, then checked the existing one instead of trusting my own. demonstration_version_space_v1 ALREADY had nth, nth_from_end, nth_slot, nearest, matches(), pick() and _same_element(). My module re-implemented shipped code.
The tree already names 1415 of 1415 actionable elements: a description that selects exactly one element exists for every single one.

The 5.43 bits came from descriptions_left, which is hypotheses still ALIVE after a demonstration. Recomputed from the learner's own descriptions_of: median 42 descriptions name one element, log2 = 5.23. It is REDUNDANCY -- 42 ways to say the same thing -- not ambiguity, and not a second grammar.
Measured on the actual preference: the description the learner prefers carries 0.102 bits and selects more than one element for only 67 of 1415 (4.7%).

what_this_is: A set-algebra audit of measured receipts against the real published corpus, using only clean held-out arms, plus an effect-based census of mechanisms already in the tree. The 24/40 union is now also one composed run under the corpus pytest, and the audit reads the later invariance, exact-decision, browser, new-environment, read-first, operand, replay-drift, trigger, long-tail, one-demonstration-basin and GUI-invariance measurements without crediting any of them as new capability.
